design: Local open-weight mirror of OpenAI GPT-Live: Moshi full-duplex FRONT delegates to a local Qwen3.5-4B GGUF reasoning brain, one RTX A5000 (GPU0).
teacher_forcing_mechanism: LMGen(on_text_hook=...) overwrites the sampled text token in place before the depformer vocalises it
pacing_note: 1 word-piece + 2 pad frames per frame (gap=2); no learned alignment model, so pacing is heuristic and audio sampling adds run-to-run variance.

examples.name: france
examples.user_transcript_asr: What is the capital of France?
examples.moshi_own_inner_monologue: Hello, how was your day? The capital of France is Paris.
examples.brain_answer: The capital of France is Paris.
examples.spoken_output_asr_verification: Paris, the capital of France is Paris. It is no

examples.name: fifa
examples.user_transcript_asr: How many times has brazen one the men's world cup and rich ears?
examples.moshi_own_inner_monologue: Hi, how is it going? She won it twice in 1980
examples.brain_answer: I don't know what you are asking because those words do not make sense.
examples.spoken_output_asr_verification: cup. I don't know what you are asking because those words do not make sense.

honest_findings: Moshi + brain load CO-RESIDENT: peak ~20.5 GB of 24 GB. Fits.

Teacher-forcing Moshi's inner monologue via LMGen(on_text_hook=...) WORKS: forced answer tokens drive the depformer, the output wav re-transcribes to the answer (France: 'the capital of France is Paris'; FIFA 15-word answer near-verbatim).

moshiko's inner monologue is Moshi's OWN reply, NOT a verbatim user ASR, and it is factually unreliable (FIFA: 'She won it twice in 1980'). Hence the delegation controller uses a separate faster-whisper ASR of the user turn, and delegates facts/reasoning to the brain -- the whole point of the architecture.
Pacing has no learned alignment model; gap=2 is the intelligibility sweet spot but audio-token sampling (temp 0.8) gives run-to-run variance and occasional word echoes/artifacts.
base.en ASR garbled the noisier FIFA input, which cascaded into the brain -- front-end ASR quality matters.
